new_senses.gloss: make disciples of, bring to the Christian faith
new_senses.rationale: Three consecutive clauses identify the saints as agents and region/people as objects; brought them to Christ’s path confirms the evangelizing event. This adds an active list beside round 1 Detransitive 1, without renumbering it.

added_examples.turoyo: Hani kulle, aq qadišani kulle, at talmiḏe d Mor Awgin wayye. W hənne yaʕni mtalmaḏḏe u Ṭurayḏan, Ṭur ʕAbdin. Kətwobe mhayəmne, kətwobe ʕamo kəfuro ste ġalabe.
added_examples.translation: All these, all these saints, were Saint Awgin's disciples. And they, that is, made disciples of our mountain region, Tur Abdin. There were believers in it; there were also many unbelieving people in it.
added_examples.rationale: New active Preterit/1: saints as agents and Tur Abdin as regional object.

added_examples.turoyo: Lənne mtalmaḏḏe taqriban u ʕamo kule. Amṭalle lu darbo d Mšiḥo. U Mor Aḥo ste ḥa manək we. Kətle ḥamməš dayroṯo, maʕmarle bu Ṭuro l Mor Aḥo.
added_examples.translation: They made disciples of almost the whole people. They brought them to Christ's path. And Saint Aho too was one of those. He has five monasteries; Saint Aho built them in the mountain region.
added_examples.rationale: New active Preterit/1: human collective object and explicit bringing to Christ’s path clarify regional metonymy.

summary: Direct restricted glossary lookups find no entry under tlmḏ or tlmd. Form mtalmḏi yields only loose consonantal candidates, none establishing this disciple lexeme.

The supplied ecclesiastical context has plural mtalmḏi parallel to mhaymanne after temporal məd clauses. No agent, object or addressee of teaching is expressed; the context favors entering discipleship, while English discipled alone does not determine voice.

Stem I and Detransitive Preterit retain the reader’s analysis provisionally. The attested root-initial t must be distinguished from any Detransitive morphology before a productive paradigm is claimed.

Only the plural form mtalmḏi is supplied. Ordinary Preterit/Infectum and singular Detransitive base forms are left unattested; no transitive make disciples sense or separate instruction sense is inferred.
The reader relates the root to ecclesiastical Aramaic vocabulary. No external etymological source was consulted and no precise source language or derivation is established here.
All three occurrences reviewed. Original glossary entry remains absent, but round 1 already proposed tlmḏ I Detransitive 1 become a disciple; that proposal is not repeated.

Jan provides the transitive counterpart that round 1 lacked: explicit hənne/lənne agents, zero-marked region and human objects, and li haymonuṯo d Mšiḥo as goal/orientation in Jan 2.13/3300. The nearby talmiḏe nominal independently fits discipleship.

Preserve the baseline stem I labeling rather than silently moving it to Q or multiplying identical stems. Four radicals motivate the reader’s Q convention, but the editorial labeling question remains open.

Attested active mtalmaḏḏe is plural. No singular Preterit/Infectum pair is invented, and the round 1 mtalmḏi Detransitive analysis remains provisional. The new explicit object contrast strengthens the lexical relationship without settling every morphophonological detail.

The first clause has an uncertain quantitative expression bam mo əšti-šawʕi. It is not needed in the two clearer added examples and is not normalized from the project English. No fixed idiom is established.
Confirm segmentation, stem and Detransitive status of mtalmḏi. Is it a productive Turoyo verb or a retained ecclesiastical predicate?
Does the speaker mean became disciples, were made disciples, or received instruction? Please establish voice from Turoyo usage rather than the ambiguous English discipled.
Elicit singular Preterit/Infectum and any ordinary-versus-Detransitive opposition before completing the base forms; confirm whether tlmḏ or tlmd is the preferred root spelling.
Confirm whether the glossary wants I or Q for this four-radical lexeme. Until then preserve round 1 I and treat Q as a labeling correction, not a new stem.
Confirm singular active base forms, L-assimilation in mtalmaḏḏe and the active/Detransitive relationship to round 1 mtalmḏi.
Clarify bam mo əšti-šawʕi at Jan 2.13/3300 before reusing its full English; no source arithmetic is repaired here.
Region as object is metonymic for its people; the adjacent human collective object makes a separate geographical evangelize sense unnecessary.
